title: Churchill and Bessie Braddock: Sober by Morning
summary: When accused of being disgustingly drunk, Churchill retorted: 'My dear, you are ugly... but tomorrow morning I shall be sober, and you will still be ugly!'
keywords: Churchill and Bessie Braddock: Sober by Morning
full_text:
Late one evening in 1946, following an exhausting debate in the House of Commons, Winston Churchill was leaving the parliamentary lobby, his steps slightly unsteady from wine.

Bessie Braddock, a formidable Labour MP renowned for her fierce socialist convictions, confronted him in the corridor.

Looking down at him with undisguised contempt, Braddock announced loudly:
"Winston, you are drunk! And what's more, you are disgustingly drunk!"

Churchill stopped, gripped his lapels, and delivered his devastating rebuttal:

**"My dear Bessie, you are ugly! And what's more, you are disgustingly ugly!
But tomorrow morning, I shall be sober... and you will still be disgustingly ugly!"**

The lobby erupted with suppressed laughter as Braddock retreated in embarrassment.

Churchill's merciless comeback demonstrated the folly of making personal attacks on an adversary endowed with lightning verbal reflexes.
moral: Those who launch personal attacks must be prepared for the consequences; wit is the deadliest counter to self-righteous judgment.
